title: Finite-field model compactified squares and geometric fibers
statement: For a finite-field datum $D=(k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $\mathrm{Models}_D$ be the full subcategory of schemes over $k_0$ whose structural morphisms are locally of finite type and quasi-compact, with all over-morphisms; no structural separatedness is imposed [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Its geometric-fiber functor is scalar extension $T_0\mapsto T_0\times_{k_0}k$ into the existing $\mathrm{SixFunctorSpace}(D)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [def-sf-operation-stages]. A model compactified square consists of $X_0,Y_0,X'_0,Y'_0,Z_0,Z'_0$ in this category, maps $f:X_0\to Y_0$, $f':X'_0\to Y'_0$, $g:Y'_0\to Y_0$, $g':X'_0\to X_0$, $i:X_0\to Z_0$, $i':X'_0\to Z'_0$, $p:Z_0\to Y_0$, $p':Z'_0\to Y'_0$, $h:Z'_0\to Z_0$, with $i,i'$ open immersions, $p,p'$ proper, $f=pi$, $f'=p'i'$, and each of the main, open and proper squares Cartesian (with its commuting over-morphism equality). Its model compactification is the specified $X_0\xrightarrow{i}Z_0\xrightarrow{p}Y_0$ [def-nagata-compactification]. Scalar extension preserves these Cartesian squares and their open/proper factors, giving the existing geometric compactified square and its chosen compactifications. A compactification of the scalar extension of a composite is transported to the composite of the scalar extensions only across the fiber functor's composition equality.
